subject.title: Subagent lifecycle observability + async supervision controls

question: Should OpenClaw define a durable subagent lifecycle receipt and audited supervision API as a core Gateway/task-ledger contract, and which lifecycle fields/actions are in scope for the first version?
rationale: The issue crosses persistent storage, Gateway protocol, task/artifact/audit boundaries, and security-sensitive control semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the stable API shape.

options.title: Design bounded core receipt API
options.body: Add a metadata-only ordered lifecycle receipt linked to tasks, artifacts, and audit records, plus audited cancel/steer/resume semantics as the core contract.

options.title: Narrow to task-ledger timeline first
options.body: Ship only durable lifecycle events and terminal guidance first, deferring steer/resume until the control semantics are separately designed.

options.title: Route richer views to plugins after seams
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only missing generic hooks and let plugins or dashboards build richer operator timelines.

recommendation.title: Design bounded core receipt API
recommendation.body: Add a metadata-only ordered lifecycle receipt linked to tasks, artifacts, and audit records, plus audited cancel/steer/resume semantics as the core contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Control UI task work and maintainer-facing product context make this the strongest available owner for choosing the core-vs-UI/API boundary.
